description: Curated parameter facts for Neural DSP Morgan Amps Suite. Hand-maintained: this is the contract the generator writes against. It contains no Neural DSP code, audio, or preset content - only parameter names, units, and ranges needed to read and write presets for a licensed copy of the plugin.

/version.note: Plugin format version. Never write this - it is the file's own schema tag.

/selectedAmp.note: Chooses the live amp. All three amp modules exist in every preset, so any template can reach any amp. User-verified in the plugin.

parameters/gateThreshold.note: No declared range. Observed around -72 dB.

pr12Amp/pr12Volume.note: PR12 is a 12W Princeton-style amp; past roughly 60% it starts to break up.

pr12Amp/pr12Dwell.note: Spring-reverb decay. Morgan added it to the original Princeton circuit specifically so you can run a high reverb mix without washing the tone out — so for a wet-but-defined clean, raise pr12Reverb and keep dwell moderate.

sw50rAmp/sw50rLevel.note: Master volume - does not add gain.

sw50rAmp/sw50rTrebleBoost.note: Front-end treble boost. The config reference calls this control `bassEmphasis` and advises using it for a thicker lead, which would be the wrong direction — the stored key name is the plugin authors' own label and is the better evidence. Treat it as a brightness/cut boost, and verify by ear.

ac20Amp/ac20Cut.note: Treble cut, borrowed from the Vox power-amp Cut control: HIGHER = DARKER. It works backwards from a normal tone knob. An earlier note in this repo claimed the opposite; the config reference, the control's name, and Morgan's own description of it as attenuating highs all agree on higher = darker. Check by ear in five seconds: raise it and listen for the top end to go.

ac20Amp/ac20BassTreble.note: Engages the cathode-follower tonestack - fuller mids, more AC30-like.

ac20Amp/ac20Power.note: Output-power mode selector; member names not yet known. Selectors are index-based (position in the control, from 0), confirmed for enums.internalMic. To fill this in: read the control's options off the plugin UI in order, write them here as members, then confirm with `scripts/probe.py --param ac20Amp/ac20Power --values <one index>`. The integer is never shown in the UI, so it cannot be read directly.

tremolo/tremoloSync.note: When on, tremoloSyncNote sets the rate and tremoloRate is ignored.

tremolo/tremoloSyncNote.note: Note-division selector; member names not yet known. Prefer `tremoloRate` in Hz with `tremoloSync` off. Selectors are index-based (position in the control, from 0), confirmed for enums.internalMic. To fill this in: read the control's options off the plugin UI in order, write them here as members, then confirm with `scripts/probe.py --param tremolo/tremoloSyncNote --values <one index>`. The integer is never shown in the UI, so it cannot be read directly.

cabParameters/leftCabPan.note: Pan position selector; member names not yet known. Selectors are index-based (position in the control, from 0), confirmed for enums.internalMic. To fill this in: read the control's options off the plugin UI in order, write them here as members, then confirm with `scripts/probe.py --param cabParameters/leftCabPan --values <one index>`. The integer is never shown in the UI, so it cannot be read directly.

cabParameters/leftChosenIRFilePath.note: Absolute path to a third-party IR on the machine that saved the preset. Empty means 'use the internal mic'. Setting it empty is irreversible in this tool: an empty value is absorbed into neighbouring marker bytes and the key stops being addressable. Use --strip-irs.

delay/delayTime.note: Used when delaySync selects free-running mode.

delay/delaySync.note: Sync-source selector (free / host tempo / tap per the config reference); member names not yet known. You usually do not need it: leave it at whatever the template has and set `delayTime` in ms. The bundled example holds 0 alongside a meaningful 420 ms delayTime, which suggests 0 is the free-running mode — an inference from one preset, not a verified fact. Selectors are index-based (position in the control, from 0), confirmed for enums.internalMic. To fill this in: read the control's options off the plugin UI in order, write them here as members, then confirm with `scripts/probe.py --param delay/delaySync --values <one index>`. The integer is never shown in the UI, so it cannot be read directly.

delay/delaySyncNote.note: Note-division selector; member names not yet known. PREFER `delayTime` IN MILLISECONDS INSTEAD: packs/timing.py converts a tempo and a division into exact ms (120 BPM + '1/8 dotted' = 375 ms), which needs no selector and leaves the delay free-running. Only use this selector when the user wants the delay to follow host tempo changes. Selectors are index-based (position in the control, from 0), confirmed for enums.internalMic. To fill this in: read the control's options off the plugin UI in order, write them here as members, then confirm with `scripts/probe.py --param delay/delaySyncNote --values <one index>`. The integer is never shown in the UI, so it cannot be read directly.
